claim: Test-case pass-rate reward does not reliably improve code RL performance over binary whole-task pass/fail reward in rigorous controlled experiments across base models and critic-free algorithms.
stance_target: naive per-requirement/per-test pass-fraction reward for code RL as a novel or reliable improvement
scope_conditions: critic-free RL (GRPO, RLOO) for code generation, multiple base models, controlled ablation
quoted_support: we study pass-rate rewards in critic-free RL for code generation (e.g., GRPO and RLOO) and report a consistent pattern across base models and algorithms: despite alleviating reward sparsity, pass-rate rewards do not reliably improve final performance over binary rewards in rigorous controlled experiments.

claim: Test-case pass rate is a miscalibrated surrogate for progress toward full correctness because partial-pass solutions within the same GRPO/RLOO group induce conflicting gradient directions that cancel out.
stance_target: assumption that denser per-test reward straightforwardly improves optimization signal in critic-free RL
scope_conditions: group-relative critic-free RL algorithms (GRPO, RLOO) for code generation
quoted_support: This arises because test-case pass rate is a miscalibrated surrogate for progress toward full correctness, and partial-pass solutions within the same group can induce conflicting gradient directions that cancel out.

claim: The paper's authors explicitly call for reward designs that better align optimization with full correctness, since dense pass-rate signal alone is insufficient.
stance_target: open problem framing for dense reward design in code RL
quoted_support: Overall, our results suggest that, in critic-free RL, pass-rate rewards are insufficient to improve code generation and motivate reward designs that better align optimization with the goal of full correctness.
